Xiaomi 18 Pro Global: Baterai Diduga Dipangkas 14-17% dari Versi China, Layar Belakang Akhirnya Go Global

Updated: November 10, 2026. We finally have a date. Xiaomi has confirmed the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max will launch globally on November 17, 2026 , at an event in Paris — a week after the company would only say "this November." The announcement came in an official post on Xiaomi's X account on Monday, November 9, and it settles the one question hanging over the phones since their China debut in September: when, and where, the rest of the world gets them. It also confirms the feature that matters most. For the first time, Xiaomi is bringing its rear display — the "Back Display" — to the global market. The 17 Pro series kept that second screen China-only last year. This time it is the headline of the launch, and Xiaomi's teaser says it plainly: "This time, there's more on the back."

There is one catch, and it is a big one for anyone who followed the China launch: the global models are widely reported to ship with smaller batteries than the Chinese versions. The Pro Max's reported global battery is about 17% smaller than the 8,500mAh cell in China. That is not confirmed by Xiaomi yet — but the reports come from EU regulatory filings, and they are consistent enough to take seriously. Everything else — the dual 200MP Leica cameras, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips, the 100W charging — is coming over unchanged, as far as we know. This is a follow-up to our first Xiaomi 18 Pro global launch story from November 3 , when the only confirmed facts were the month and the lineup. This article covers what is new since then: the date, the venue, the global-first rear display, and the battery question. Xiaomi's post on X, published November 9, 2026, reads in full: "Back for more! The all-new Xiaomi 18 Pro Series comes in two sizes, both with flagship tech and imaging. And this time, there's more on the back. Say hello to the innovative Back Display. It's made to shoot better, stand out, and do more. See you in Paris on November 17th at..."

The two sizes are the Xiaomi 18 Pro (6.4-inch display) and the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (6.9-inch display). There is no vanilla Xiaomi 18 at this event — the standard model is expected to debut separately, with tipsters pointing to December and Xiaomi president Lu Weibing confirming it arrives later. That is the same pattern as last year, when only the Pro models went global in the first wave. Xiaomi also teased "more surprises" for the November 17 event without saying what they are. That could mean accessories, the rumoured telephoto extender kit, or something else entirely — we will find out next week. GSMArena already has global review units in hand (its Pro Max is a Velvet Red 12GB/256GB model) and says it aims to publish its full review around launch day, which means the phones are real, finished hardware, not prototypes. The rear display is the single most interesting thing about this launch, and the reason Xiaomi is leading with it. The 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max had a small second screen built into the camera island, but Xiaomi never sold those phones outside China. The 18 Pro series is the first time the feature leaves China — and Xiaomi clearly thinks it is the selling point, putting it in the launch teaser ahead of the cameras and the chips. On the Chinese models, the rear screen is 2.7 inches on the 18 Pro and 2.9 inches on the 18 Pro Max , running at 120Hz. It is, in GSMArena's words, "a camera-island-shaped smartwatch on the back of the phone": you can check notifications, answer calls, control music, check the weather and calendar, set a timer — and, most usefully, frame selfies with the main rear cameras instead of the front camera. That last trick is the one Xiaomi keeps showing off in its hands-on coverage, and it is genuinely useful: a 200MP main camera takes a far better selfie than any front camera. Xiaomi is also teasing new privacy displays for the global models, according to Android Headlines' report on the announcement — a display that narrows the viewing angle so people next to you cannot read your screen. That is a practical feature for a phone this expensive, and it fits the "flagship tech" framing of the launch. The hardware is unchanged from the China launch on September 23, 2026, and everything below is confirmed from that event and Xiaomi's own materials:

The dual 200MP Leica setup is the camera story: a 200MP main sensor and a 200MP periscope telephoto, with a 50MP ultra-wide reported in coverage of the China models. The chips are Qualcomm's newest 2nm parts — the standard 8 Elite Gen 6 in the Pro, the higher-clocked 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 in the Pro Max — the same silicon family as the Motorola Signature 27 , which launched at $1,599.99 in the US last week. And both models charge at 100W wired and 50W wireless, which is faster than anything Apple or Samsung sells. For context on where this sits in the market: the 18 Pro Max is Xiaomi's answer to the iPhone 18 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra class — dual 200MP cameras, a second display, and a battery that, even in its smaller global form, is far bigger than either rival's. The China price of about $840 for the base Pro is aggressive; the global price, as always with Xiaomi, will be higher. How much higher is the open question. Here is the part to watch. Multiple reports citing EU EPREL regulatory filings say the global 18 Pro will carry a battery of about 6,000mAh instead of the 7,000mAh cell in the Chinese model, and the global Pro Max about 7,050mAh instead of 8,500mAh. That would be a cut of roughly 14% on the Pro and 17% on the Pro Max. This is not confirmed by Xiaomi. It comes from regulatory filings and supply-chain reports, and Xiaomi has not commented. But the pattern is familiar: Chinese-market flagships routinely ship with larger silicon-carbon batteries than their global versions, because of different certification rules and shipping regulations for high-capacity cells. The OnePlus 16 , for example, has a 9,000mAh battery in China that is expected to shrink for other markets. Even at the reported smaller sizes, these are still very large batteries — 6,000mAh is bigger than the iPhone 18 Pro's cell and bigger than most 2026 flagships. The Pro Max at 7,050mAh would still be the biggest battery in any mainstream global flagship. The cut matters more as a signal: the headline 8,500mAh figure that Xiaomi marketed in China will not be the number on the box in Paris. If battery life is your reason for buying this phone, wait for the November 17 event and the first reviews before deciding — GSMArena's review, due around launch day, should confirm the real global capacities. Chinese prices are official and straightforward. The base 12GB/256GB models are CNY 5,999 (about $840) for the 18 Pro and CNY 6,999 (about $980) for the Pro Max, with top configurations reaching CNY 9,999 (about $1,400) for a 16GB/1TB Pro Max. Global prices have not been announced, and the leaks disagree with each other — which is exactly why none of them should be treated as fact:

All figures in this table are unconfirmed retailer leaks, not Xiaomi prices. Euro figures converted at roughly $1.13 per euro. Xiaomi announces official global pricing on November 17. What the leaks agree on is the direction: global prices will be far above the China prices — roughly $1,575 to $1,630 for the base Pro, against $840 in China. That is the usual Xiaomi global markup (taxes, certification, distribution, and a different channel model), but it is steeper than usual, and it tracks the wider 2026 trend: memory prices are climbing fast, and every flagship launching this year costs more than its predecessor. Our iPhone 18 Pro storage analysis showed Apple's flash costs up 4.5x year on year; the same memory crunch is pushing Xiaomi's prices up too. Expect the official Paris prices to land near the top of the leaked range — and expect the usual launch-week deals to soften them within a month. The 18 Pro series is Xiaomi's most serious attempt yet to be taken as a global flagship brand rather than a value alternative. The rear display is a genuine differentiator — no other global flagship has one — and the dual 200MP Leica cameras and 2nm chips put it on paper ahead of the iPhone 18 Pro and the Galaxy S27 Ultra in several areas. The Paris event is also a statement: Xiaomi is launching its best phones in Europe's fashion capital, not in Beijing, and aiming them squarely at buyers who would otherwise buy Apple or Samsung. The risk is the price. At a leaked €1,399 (about $1,575) for the base Pro, Xiaomi is asking iPhone money for a phone most European buyers have never owned — and the smaller reported battery takes away the one spec that most obviously justified the premium over an iPhone. If the official price lands at the top of the leaked range, the 18 Pro Max at around $2,000 would be competing with the Motorola Signature 27 ($1,599.99) and the iPhone 18 Pro ($1,199) on brand trust, not specs. If it lands lower, it undercuts both on hardware and becomes the value flagship of the year. For buyers in the UAE and the wider region, the practical advice is simple: watch the November 17 event for the official prices and the confirmed global battery sizes, and wait for the first reviews before buying. The phones are real, the launch is a week away, and the two numbers that matter — price and battery — are the two numbers we still don't have. We will update this article when Xiaomi confirms them. And if you are sourcing units for resale, run an IMEI check on any unit before you pay — global and China variants will look identical in the hand, but they may differ in battery, bands and warranty, and that difference is worth real money. November 17, 2026, at a launch event in Paris. Xiaomi confirmed the date on its official X account on November 9, 2026. The sale date has not been announced yet — November 17 is the launch event, not necessarily the first day of sales. Two: the Xiaomi 18 Pro (6.4-inch display) and the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (6.9-inch display). The vanilla Xiaomi 18 is not part of this event and is expected to debut separately, reportedly in December. A second screen built into the camera island on the back of the phone — 2.7 inches on the 18 Pro, 2.9 inches on the Pro Max, both 120Hz. It shows notifications, calls, music, weather and calendar, and lets you frame selfies with the main rear cameras. It was China-only on the 17 Pro series; the 18 Pro is the first time it goes global. Not announced yet. In China the base 12GB/256GB models cost about $840 (18 Pro) and $980 (Pro Max). Unconfirmed retailer leaks put the global Pro at roughly $1,575-$1,630 and the Pro Max at roughly $1,795-$2,010, but the leaks disagree with each other. Official prices come on November 17. Reported, not confirmed. EU regulatory filings cited by multiple outlets point to about 6,000mAh for the global Pro (vs 7,000mAh in China) and about 7,050mAh for the global Pro Max (vs 8,500mAh in China). Xiaomi has not confirmed this. Even at those sizes, both would still be among the biggest batteries in any global flagship. India was not named among the launch regions, and reports of a December India launch are unconfirmed. The Middle East has been named as a target region in reports, but no UAE date or price has been announced. Expect grey-market units in Dubai before any official UAE launch. Sources: Xiaomi official X account (November 9, 2026); Android Headlines (November 9/10, 2026); GSMArena "Xiaomi 18 Pro Max in for review" (November 9, 2026); TechTimes (November 2, 2026); Pandromeda. Prices converted at roughly 7.14 yuan per dollar and $1.13 per euro, November 10, 2026. Global battery and price figures are unconfirmed reports, labelled as such in the article.
